cards.definition: To get or pick up something, or to use a form of transport.

example.text: You took the wrong key.

cards.definition: To speak to someone, or to have a conversation.

example.text: It's been nice talking to you, but I really must go now.

cards.definition: Having a greater than average height.

example.text: Bill is not tall like you.

cards.definition: A hot drink made by pouring hot water over dried leaves.

example.text: Would you like coffee or tea?

cards.definition: To give knowledge or skills to someone.

example.text: Teach me how you do it.

cards.definition: A person whose job is to teach students, especially in a school.

example.text: Mr Kato is a teacher.

cards.definition: To give information to someone by speaking or writing.

example.text: Please tell us where there is a grocery store.

cards.definition: An examination to see how much you know or can do.

example.text: Tom made some mistakes in the test.

cards.definition: To express gratitude or appreciation to someone.

example.text: You ought to thank him.

cards.definition: Used to point to a specific thing or person far away from you.

example.text: Look at that big tree.

cards.definition: Used before a noun when you are talking about a specific thing or person.

example.text: Could you dial for me? The telephone is too high.

cards.definition: Belonging to or connected with them.

example.text: It is the students' duty to clean their classrooms.

cards.definition: At that time, or next in a sequence of events.

example.text: Just then, the bus stopped.

cards.definition: In, at, or to that place.

example.text: Open the cupboard to the left, the bottles are in there.

cards.definition: People, animals, or things that have been mentioned before.

example.text: Are they all the same?

cards.definition: An object, idea, or action that is not alive.

example.text: Don't buy things on credit.

cards.definition: To form an idea or opinion in your mind.

example.text: I think I have a theory about that.

cards.definition: Used to point to a specific thing or person near you.

example.text: Why do you want to buy this book?

cards.definition: The period during which something happens or exists.

example.text: What time will you leave?

cards.definition: Feeling that you want to rest or sleep.

example.text: Why are you so tired today?

cards.definition: On this present day.

example.text: Who else is gone today?

cards.definition: The day after today.

example.text: The rent is due tomorrow.

cards.definition: On the evening of the present day.

example.text: What are you going to do tonight?

cards.definition: More than is needed or wanted; also.

example.text: Your hair is too long.

cards.definition: A place where people live and work, smaller than a city.

example.text: I saw a town in the distance.

cards.definition: A vehicle that runs on rails, carrying passengers or goods.

example.text: The train was due at six.

cards.definition: A tall plant with a thick stem and branches.

example.text: It's fruit fresh from the tree.

cards.definition: To attempt to do something.

example.text: Students should try not to be late.

cards.definition: To move around a central point; to change direction.

example.text: Turn your face this way.

cards.definition: In a position directly below something.

example.text: It is under the chair.

cards.definition: To know the meaning of something or how something works.

example.text: I understand how you feel.

cards.definition: Towards a higher place or position.

example.text: Look up to the skies.

cards.definition: To take something and do something with it for a purpose.

example.text: Can I use your pen?

cards.definition: Used to make an adjective or adverb stronger.

example.text: You write a very good hand.

cards.definition: To stay in one place or not do something until something else happens.

example.text: Please wait for me at the station.

cards.definition: To move forward by putting one foot in front of the other.

example.text: Will you walk down to the school with me?

cards.definition: To have a desire or wish for something.

example.text: What do you want now?

cards.definition: A little hot, not cold.

example.text: Scotland can be very warm in September.

cards.definition: To clean something with water and often soap.

example.text: Wash your hands before eating.

cards.definition: To look at something for a period of time, often to see what happens.

example.text: Did you watch the game?

cards.definition: The clear liquid that has no color, taste, or smell, and is essential for life.

example.text: What a waste of water!

cards.definition: A path or route; a method or style of doing something.

example.text: You are in my way.

cards.definition: You and one or more other people.

example.text: Why don't we go home?

cards.definition: The conditions outside, like sun, rain, or wind.

example.text: Bad weather discouraged them from going on a picnic.

cards.definition: A period of seven days.

example.text: There are seven days in a week.

cards.definition: The days of Saturday and Sunday.

example.text: See you on the weekend.

cards.definition: In a good or satisfactory way.

example.text: She speaks English very well.

cards.definition: Asking for information about a thing or action.

example.text: What grade are you in?

cards.definition: At what time, or at the time that.

example.text: When will you be free?

cards.definition: Asking about the place something is or goes.

example.text: Where do you come from?

cards.definition: Used to ask or talk about one or more things from a group.

example.text: Which way is the beach?

cards.definition: The color of fresh snow or milk.

example.text: The doctor was wearing a white coat over a blue suit.

cards.definition: Used to ask about a person, or to refer to a person.

example.text: Do you know who he is?

cards.definition: For what reason or purpose.

example.text: Why do you think so?

cards.definition: The woman a man is married to.

example.text: Please come over with your wife.

cards.definition: An opening in a wall or door, usually with glass, to let in light.

example.text: The room has two windows.

cards.definition: The coldest season of the year, after autumn and before spring.

example.text: It was a very cold winter.

cards.definition: An adult female person.

example.text: A woman fell from a ship into the sea.

cards.definition: A single unit of language that has meaning and can be spoken or written.

example.text: You've left out a word in copying the textbook.

cards.definition: To do a job, usually to earn money.

example.text: He works for a bank.

cards.definition: The planet Earth, and all the people and things on it.

example.text: English is by far the most widely-spoken language in the world.

cards.definition: Used to talk about possible situations or to make polite requests.

example.text: Would you like to come?

cards.definition: To make letters or words on a surface, usually with a pen or pencil.

example.text: I will wait till you have written the letter.

cards.definition: A period of 365 or 366 days, divided into 12 months.

example.text: I had a stroke last year.

cards.definition: The day before today.

example.text: Why were you absent yesterday?

cards.definition: The person or people being spoken to.

example.text: You are in my way.

cards.definition: Not old; in an early stage of life or development.

example.text: Of course, I'm young, and politics is conducted by grown-ups.

cards.definition: Belonging to or connected with you.

example.text: Did you do your homework by yourself?
